import.title: Import leads from another CRM
import.intro: Bring over the contacts from the CRM you use today. Export a CSV there, upload it here, and check which column is which before anything gets saved.
import.howto1: 1. In your CRM look for “Export” and pick CSV format.
import.howto2: 2. Upload that file here (up to 5,000 contacts at a time).
import.howto3: 3. Confirm the column mapping — only then does it import.
import.csvOnly: Only .csv — if it is in Excel, use “Save as > CSV”.
import.readError: The file could not be read.
import.importError: The import could not be completed.
import.foundRows_one: We found {{count}} contact in the file.

import.truncated_one: There is {{count}} extra row: only the first 5,000 will be imported. Split the file to bring the rest.
import.truncated_other: There are {{count}} extra rows: only the first 5,000 will be imported. Split the file to bring the rest.
import.prefixHint: Used only for numbers that arrive without a country code.
import.duplicates: If the contact already exists here

import.sourceHint: Saved on every lead so you know where it came from. Optional.

import.contactHint: Off, the contacts are just stored and nobody gets a message. On, the agent starts one conversation per minute (never with the ones closed as won or lost).
import.needContactColumn: Point at least one column to phone or email: without that there is nobody to contact.
import.doneQuiet: Done. The contacts are stored and nobody was messaged: the agent will act when you decide, or when they write first.
import.doneContacting: Done. The agent will start messaging them one per minute.

domain.title: Your domain
domain.subdomainHint: We recommend a subdomain, for example notifications.yourcompany.com: that way the reputation of these sends doesn't affect your corporate email.
domain.ownerOnly: Only the account owner can add a domain.
domain.added: Domain added. Create the DNS records below.
domain.dnsHelp: Create them wherever you manage your domain's DNS (for example, Cloudflare or your hosting provider). We check every 10 minutes: as soon as we detect them, emails start going out from your domain.
domain.verifyStarted: Done: we're checking the DNS records.
domain.removeConfirm: Remove {{domain}}? Emails will go back to the shared domain, if available.

domainHelp.not_started: Verification hasn't started. Create the records and press "Verify now".
domainHelp.pending: Looking for the DNS records. It can take from minutes up to 72 hours after you create them.
domainHelp.verified: Domain verified: emails go out from here.
domainHelp.partially_verified: Domain verified: emails go out from here.
domainHelp.partially_failed: Some records couldn't be verified. Check them and press "Verify now".
domainHelp.failed: We didn't find the records within 72 hours. Check they're created correctly and press "Verify now".
domainHelp.temporary_failure: We stopped detecting the DNS records. While you check, emails go out from the shared domain.

intro.whatsapp: For {{provider}} to deliver your customers' messages, set this up in its dashboard:

meta.secret: The signing secret is your app's App Secret (App settings → Basic): paste it below, in "Webhook signing secret", and save.

elevenlabs.variables: The agent's prompt and greeting can use these variables; we fill them in on every call:
elevenlabs.overrides: If you picked a voice, greeting, language or speed in Settings, enable them in the agent's Security tab. Otherwise the call still goes out with the agent's own settings.

vapi.url: In Vapi, in your assistant, paste this Server URL:

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp
whatsapp.hint: Your YCloud (or Meta) account and your number. Needed to send/receive WhatsApp messages and create templates.
whatsapp.webhookSecretHint: Required to receive messages. YCloud: the "secret" it gives you when creating the Webhook Endpoint. Meta: your app's App Secret (Settings → Basic). Without it, inbound messages are rejected.

email.hint: Your Resend (or SMTP) account to send emails.

voice.webhookSecretHint: Required to receive call results. Vapi: the assistant's "Server URL Secret". ElevenLabs: the post-call webhook HMAC secret. Retell does not need it: it signs with the API key.

crm.label: CRM
crm.hint: Connect your CRM (HubSpot, Pipedrive, Salesforce, whatever you use) via a webhook — usually the trigger of an n8n/Zapier flow that maps the event to your CRM. The agent reports status changes, scheduled appointments, and payment promises; it can optionally look up live data from it during the conversation.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: This platform captures your leads and talks to them over WhatsApp, email and calls. Let me show you where everything is.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.body: The home screen. Ask it how to use the panel or have it create an agent: it puts together a proposal and you confirm. It never acts on its own.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.body: Every live conversation. Open a lead to see the thread, take control and reply yourself, or bring your base over from another CRM.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.body: What the agent is allowed to look up. Load your documents and exact facts like prices and hours: beyond this, it invents nothing.

agents.title: Agents and prompts
agents.body: Who handles what, and how. Set type, channels and follow-up cadence; under Prompts you tune their rules, in versions.

improve.title: Approval and metrics
improve.body: Conversations are reviewed nightly and improvements proposed. Nothing lands without your sign-off. Metrics shows how it is going.

schedule.title: Calendar and templates
schedule.body: Appointments the agent books and the ones you book, in one place. WhatsApp templates let you write outside the 24-hour window.

setup.title: Integrations and settings
setup.body: Connect your WhatsApp, email and voice accounts, and set hours, time zone and the agent voice. This is what to get done first.

help.title: Help
help.body: The full panel guide, section by section. From there you can replay this tour whenever you want.
